experimentSuggestions.title: Additive-assisted hepatocyte attachment and function benchmark on a fixed base cryomix
experimentSuggestions.hypothesis: Several hepatocyte papers imply that post-thaw attachment and function gains come from adjuncts added around a standard DMSO-centered mix rather than from new base CPA chemistry.
experimentSuggestions.rationale: Trehalose, serum, ROCK inhibitor, antioxidant, and other adjunct-style titles recur in the hepatocyte slice, but they are not benchmarked against one another on the same base protocol. Holding the core cryomix fixed and comparing post-thaw attachment and function would test whether the additive signal is real.

experimentSuggestions.title: Promote hepatocyte function-heavy protocols to transplantation endpoints
experimentSuggestions.hypothesis: Several hepatocyte protocols that look promising on attachment or in-vitro metabolic function will reorder once they are compared on engraftment or transplantation outcomes.
experimentSuggestions.rationale: The hepatocyte slice labels function more often than transplantation. Converting the strongest in-vitro function protocols into a small engraftment benchmark is likely higher-signal than inventing a new chemistry path immediately.

experimentSuggestions.title: Full-text protocol resolution for sparse hepatocyte thaw/loading workflows
experimentSuggestions.hypothesis: A number of hepatocyte papers look relevant, but their step structure is too thin to compare fairly against the rest of the corpus.
experimentSuggestions.rationale: The hepatocyte slice is provisional and abstract-level, and its weak points concentrate in papers where only thawing or one procedural phase is explicit. Full-text resolution there is likely higher signal than another broad extraction pass.

experimentSuggestions.title: Scale-up benchmark for banked or bulk hepatocyte handling
experimentSuggestions.hypothesis: Scale-up losses in hepatocyte banking may come from handling and thaw workflow variance rather than core cryomix choice alone.
experimentSuggestions.rationale: The hepatocyte corpus includes banking, bulk, and large-scale titles, but those papers are scattered across sparse workflow descriptions. A scale-up benchmark focused on loading, storage, thaw, and handling variance would test whether operational workflow dominates the observed attachment losses.

experimentSuggestions.title: Additive-assisted hepatocyte attachment and function benchmark on a fixed base cryomix
experimentSuggestions.hypothesis: Several hepatocyte papers imply that post-thaw attachment and function gains come from adjuncts added around a standard DMSO-centered mix rather than from new base CPA chemistry.
experimentSuggestions.rationale: Trehalose, serum, ROCK inhibitor, antioxidant, and other adjunct-style titles recur in the hepatocyte slice, but they are not benchmarked against one another on the same base protocol. Holding the core cryomix fixed and comparing post-thaw attachment and function would test whether the additive signal is real.

experimentSuggestions.title: Promote hepatocyte function-heavy protocols to transplantation endpoints
experimentSuggestions.hypothesis: Several hepatocyte protocols that look promising on attachment or in-vitro metabolic function will reorder once they are compared on engraftment or transplantation outcomes.
experimentSuggestions.rationale: The hepatocyte slice labels function more often than transplantation. Converting the strongest in-vitro function protocols into a small engraftment benchmark is likely higher-signal than inventing a new chemistry path immediately.

experimentSuggestions.hypothesis: A number of hepatocyte papers look relevant, but their step structure is too thin to compare fairly against the rest of the corpus.
experimentSuggestions.rationale: The hepatocyte slice is provisional and abstract-level, and its weak points concentrate in papers where only thawing or one procedural phase is explicit. Full-text resolution there is likely higher signal than another broad extraction pass.

experimentSuggestions.title: Scale-up benchmark for banked or bulk hepatocyte handling
experimentSuggestions.hypothesis: Scale-up losses in hepatocyte banking may come from handling and thaw workflow variance rather than core cryomix choice alone.
experimentSuggestions.rationale: The hepatocyte corpus includes banking, bulk, and large-scale titles, but those papers are scattered across sparse workflow descriptions. A scale-up benchmark focused on loading, storage, thaw, and handling variance would test whether operational workflow dominates the observed attachment losses.
